goal: Implement to_roman(n: int) -> str in roman_numerals.py, converting integers 1 to 3999 to Roman numerals with subtractive notation and raising ValueError for anything else.
behaviors: to_roman(1) returns "I" and to_roman(3) returns "III" (repeated additive symbols for units).
to_roman(58) returns "LVIII" and to_roman(3888) returns "MMMDCCCLXXXVIII" (additive notation across all symbols I, V, X, L, C, D, M).
to_roman(4) returns "IV" and to_roman(9) returns "IX" (subtractive notation for units).
to_roman(40) returns "XL", to_roman(90) returns "XC", to_roman(400) returns "CD" and to_roman(900) returns "CM" (subtractive notation for tens and hundreds).
to_roman(1994) returns "MCMXCIV" and to_roman(3999) returns "MMMCMXCIX" (mixed subtractive cases and upper bound).
to_roman(0), to_roman(-1) and to_roman(4000) each raise ValueError.

assumptions.text: roman_numerals.py exists in the repo root as the single flat implementation module.
The tests/ folder exists where the pytest test file will go.
pyproject.toml exists to configure the project and toolchain.
pytest is available to run the tests.
assumptions.probe: python -m pytest --version || .venv/bin/python -m pytest --version || uv run pytest --version

assumptions.text: roman_numerals.py can be imported from the repo root.

demo: python -c 'from roman_numerals import to_roman; print(to_roman(4)); print(to_roman(1994))'
out_of_scope: Converting Roman numerals back to integers
Handling non-int inputs such as strings or floats beyond what the range check naturally does
Numbers above 3999 using overline or vinculum notation
